blocks.sig: say in pairs: how would you say these in english? take turns. don't worry about mistakes — we'll come back to them later.
text leo and his gran look at her old photos. read their conversation with the glossary. who are you more like — margaret or leo? tell each other why: give two reasons. photos-main.jpg
say look again. how do they say when? discuss together, then tap “show the answer”.
say 🔁 back to the start: how would you say these now? take turns. then tap “show the answer”.
game memo: look at the phrases for 40 seconds and try to remember them. then they disappear: take turns and say one each — in a sentence about you.
text remember the missing words and say them. tap the yellow and orange to check.
text now without the glossary.
cards margaret and leo: ask and answer about them. take turns: one asks with when did…?, the next answers from memory. then tap the card.
game noughts and crosses: pick a square. grey = could be better, green = good; a red word = use it. say the sentence in perfect english, then tap to check. three in a row wins!
game the wheel of questions: take turns to spin. make the question and ask the next person. they answer: yes, i did / no, i didn't + one detail. then tap to check the question.
model here's how it works. complete the chats. then tap the yellow to check.

game snakes and ladders: take turns to roll the dice and move. on your square, ask the next person: when did you…? tap to check your question. then they answer with a time phrase (from the box or your own: in my mid-twenties, two years ago; not sure? i can't remember exactly — at ten, maybe?) + one detail.
questions now your real stories.
game the wheel of questions: take turns to spin. ask the next person: when did you last…? they answer (last month, ages ago, at school…) + one detail. then tap to check your question.
text leo and his gran look at her old photos. read the first part of their conversation with the glossary. photos-main.jpg
text read on. who are you more like — margaret or leo? tell each other why: give two reasons.
say look at the bold phrases from the conversation. how do they say when? discuss each question, then tap “show the answer”.
box the language for today. read it together: which phrases were in leo and margaret's conversation?
text the second part: remember the missing words and say them. tap the yellow and orange to check.
text now without the glossary: the second part.
postits share with your partner. old-photos.jpg
say agree or disagree — gently. take turns. read out a statement as if it's your own opinion, with the tag. your partner gently agrees or disagrees, using a phrase from the box, and gives one reason.
say more statements. take turns, as before.
say more statements. take turns, as before.

my husband and i visited it only once, about ten years ago. про одну страну: были там один раз, лет десять назад my husband and i have visited it only once, about ten years ago. when did you last go somewhere new? tell each other two things you remember about it. “ten years ago” — это «когда?», и это уже в прошлом → past simple. “only once” — отлично.

i went to an art museum a week ago. ходили в музей неделю назад i 've been to an art museum a week ago. when did you last go to a museum or a gallery? name one thing you remember — or one you'd like to see. с “ago” — только past simple: не have been и не was to → went.

did you go to a concert or a festival this summer? сейчас ноябрь: спрашиваете друга о лете did you went to a concert or a festival this summer? did you go anywhere special this summer? tell each other about one place (even a park or a café near home). после “did” — всегда базовая форма: did + go. лето закончилось → past simple.

yeah, i enjoyed it. друг спрашивает про ваши прошлые выходные yeah, i 've enjoyed this. how was your last weekend? say two things you did. выходные закончились → past simple, даже без даты. и “it”, а не “this”: о том, что уже было.

i learned to ride a bike as a kid. i learned to ride a bike when i was a child. ^^kid^^ when did you learn to swim or ride a bike? who taught you? tell each other one funny or scary moment. “as a kid” = в детстве; так говорят чаще, чем “in my childhood”. or: when i was a kid — тоже верно.

i left home at 18. i left home when i was eighteen. ^^at^^ when did you first live away from your parents — or do you still live with them? name one good thing and one hard thing about it. в 18 лет → “at 18”, не in 18.

i found a job right out of college. / i found a job straight out of university. i found a job as soon as i graduated. ^^out^^ what did you do right after high school — study, work or something else? why? сразу после вуза: “right out of college” (us) или “straight out of university” (uk) — выбирай свой вариант. or: right after university.

i met my best friend in my third year at university. / i met my best friend in my third year of college. i met my best friend when i was a third-year student at university. ^^my^^ where and when did you meet one of your oldest friends? say one thing you did together back then. на третьем курсе: “at university” (uk) или “of college” (us), не on the third course.

i still can't drive. i haven't learned to drive yet. ^^still^^ name one thing you still don't have (a car, a dog, a garden…). do you want it? why or why not? до сих пор не умею → “i still can't” — это правда и сейчас. or: i still haven't learned to drive.

where did this happen? сосед рассказывает про кражу в доме where did this happened? tell each other about one surprising thing that happened near your home. when and where did it happen? после “did” — базовая форма: did + happen.
did anybody get hurt? друг рассказал про аварию did anybody got hurt? tell each other about a small accident you saw or heard about (a bike, the kitchen…). did anyone get hurt? did + get, не got.

did they steal anything? соседку обокрали did they stole anything? tell each other about a theft you heard about (on the news or near you). what did they steal? did + steal; “stole” — только без “did”: they stole my bike.

i bought my first car in my late thirties. i bought my first car when i was 37. ^^late^^ what did you do in your early twenties? name two things — and one you'd do differently now. 37–39 → “in my late thirties”; 34–36 → “mid-thirties”; 30–33 → “early thirties”.

i moved to a new city in my mid-twenties. i moved to a new city when i was about 25. ^^mid^^ where did you live in your mid-twenties? say one thing you liked about it and one you didn't. около 25 → “in my mid-twenties” (mid- с дефисом).

i worked in a shop after i left school. i worked in a shop when i finished school. ^^left^^ what did you do after you left school? tell each other one good and one bad thing about it. после окончания школы: “after i left school” (uk) = “after high school” (us). не путай с “after school” — после уроков.

i haven't been to the theatre for ages. давно не были в театре i haven't been to the theatre ages. name one thing you haven't done for ages but would like to do again. why haven't you? давно не… → “haven't … for ages” (present perfect). а «сто лет назад» → “ages ago” (past simple): i went there ages ago.

i lost it a few years ago. потеряла кольцо несколько лет назад i lost it few years ago. tell each other about something you lost a few years ago. did you ever find it? “a few” = несколько; “few” без “a” = мало.
